outcome.technical:
The product WAS affected. audit-lookup.py `brief --read` printed the brief with sys.stdout.write(text). On Windows a text stdout turns every 
 into 
, and its encoding is the console code page. A reviewer brief embeds the executor's filed return as filed, and a return filed on Windows carries CRLF: subprocess on Windows writes `input=` through a TextIOWrapper that turns 
 into 
, and run_verb hands the return to file-return that way. So each embedded CRLF line came out as 
. drive-phase run_brief's universal-newline capture then read that as two newlines, while sn6 read the file as one. That explains (4, [True, False, True, False]): the executor briefs embed no filed return. Probe on macOS: the reviewer brief from a two-task --signal drive holds 0 CR and 0 non-ASCII here, so sn6 is green on POSIX. The Windows half is reasoned from CPython's subprocess source (Popen.__init__ wraps stdin in TextIOWrapper(newline=None); _stdin_write writes through it). It was not observed on a Windows host. Fix: new audit-lookup.write_exact(stream, text) writes the UTF-8 bytes to stream.buffer after a flush. A stream with no buffer (StringIO) gets the text, which it neither translates nor encodes, so bo2 is unchanged. New case in test_audit_lookup _brief_cases: a filed return with CRLF and U+2190 gives a reviewer brief. It is read through main --read under redirect_stdout(io.TextIOWrapper(BytesIO, encoding='cp1252', errors='strict', newline='
')), and the bytes printed must equal the file's bytes. Before the fix it raised UnicodeEncodeError (red; 99/100). After the fix it passes (100/100). Second-direction mutant, run in a scratch copy and not in the tree: write_exact replaced by reconfigure-to-utf-8 plus a text write goes red with 3543 vs 3490 bytes and 3 
, so the CRLF half is held separately. drive-phase.py's own writes: none of its open() calls is a text-mode open without an encoding, so it is unchanged. test_drive_phase.py: new unencoded_text_opens(source), an AST walk reporting the line of each open()/io.open() in text mode with no encoding=. A new case in sb-block runs it over governance/drive-phase.py and tests/test_drive_phase.py, plus a seven-line twin (lines 1,2,3,6 reported; 4,5,7 not). It was red first with 68 sites, all in the test file, _write_lf among them (the fm-block cp1252 crash). Every site now names encoding='utf-8'. Mutants (none / every open / ignore encoding) each give a twin answer other than [1,2,3,6]. Also set encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' on the four subprocess captures of verb/driver/hook output in that file, which decoded UTF-8 output in the locale encoding. test_audit_task.py tk7: pc_gone_pid now keeps each exited Popen in a list for the life of the block. On Windows an open process handle keeps the pid from being reused; before this, the Popen was collected on return and its handle closed. No POSIX red is possible for this. Runs: test_audit_lookup 100/100 (also under PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252); test_drive_phase --stage sb-block --stage sn5-block 9/9 under cp1252; full sweep 335/335 files ok, exit 0; ruff and vermin exit 0.
outcome.descriptive: brief --read now prints a brief's exact bytes on any platform and stdout encoding, so Windows reviewer briefs are no longer mangled. The drive's test fixtures write UTF-8 under a lint that names any open without an encoding, and tk7's dead pid can no longer be reused on Windows.
